constraints: integer comparisons; include negatives
hints: Locate both integers on a number line; numbers farther right are greater.
Pay attention to signs: every negative number lies left of every positive number.
Does the ordering on the number line satisfy the direction of the displayed comparison?

objective: Test a value in an inequality
constraints: substitute and compare; yes/no answers
hints: Replace x with the proposed number in the left side of the inequality.
Calculate that left-side value before comparing it with the number on the right.
The proposed value belongs in the solution set when the resulting comparison is true.

constraints: contrast strict vs inclusive at the boundary
hints: Find the value where the two sides would be equal; that is the boundary.
Look at the inequality symbol: symbols with an equal bar include the boundary.
State the boundary and inclusion separately, using the symbol rather than a nearby test value.

constraints: closed for <= or >=; open for < or >
hints: Identify whether the inequality symbol includes an equal sign.
Use a filled endpoint when equality is allowed and a hollow endpoint when it is excluded.
Match the endpoint style to the exact symbol before considering which way the ray goes.

constraints: > and >= point right; < and <= point left
hints: Read the boundary number next to x.
Values greater than the boundary lie to its right on a number line; smaller values lie to its left.
Give that boundary together with the ray direction indicated by the comparison.

objective: Read the inequality from a graph
constraints: single ray; integer endpoint
hints: Read the endpoint number from the circle and note whether the circle is filled.
A ray extending left describes numbers less than the endpoint.
Combine the leftward direction with the filled-circle inclusion to write the inequality.

objective: Add or subtract on both sides
constraints: integer constants; keep the inequality direction
hints: Undo the added constant by adding its opposite to both sides.
Perform the same operation on each side while leaving the comparison symbol pointing the same way.
Check the boundary by putting it into the original inequality.

objective: Multiply or divide by a positive
constraints: positive coefficients only; no sign flips
hints: The variable is divided by a positive number.
Multiply both sides by that same positive number to isolate x.
Keep the comparison direction and test the boundary in the original statement.

constraints: pair the solution with its number-line picture
hints: Solve the inequality by undoing the constant on both sides.
Use the equality boundary as the endpoint, and notice that the equal bar determines a filled circle.
Choose the left or right ray by asking which side of the boundary makes the original inequality true.

objective: Two steps with a positive coefficient
constraints: undo addition first, then division; positive coefficients
hints: Remove the added constant before dealing with the coefficient of x.
Divide both sides by the positive coefficient after the constant has been removed.
Check the boundary in the original inequality and keep the symbol direction unchanged.

constraints: unit-fraction coefficients; integer answers
hints: Add the constant needed to leave the fraction containing x by itself.
Multiply both sides by the positive denominator to recover x.
Verify the boundary in the original inequality before writing the solution direction.

constraints: check the boundary value against strictness
hints: Solve the inequality using inverse operations in reverse order.
Use the resulting boundary to test the specified value in the original inequality.
Decide inclusion from that substitution, remembering that an equal bar permits equality.

objective: Flip the sign for a negative coefficient
constraints: reverse the inequality when dividing/multiplying by a negative
hints: Move the constant so the term containing x is alone.
When dividing by the negative coefficient, reverse the comparison symbol.
Check a value on the proposed solution side in the original inequality to confirm the direction.

constraints: simplify both sides first; flip only for a negative divisor
hints: Expand the parentheses and combine like terms on each side first.
Collect variable terms so the final coefficient of x is easy to identify.
Reverse the comparison only if the final isolation step divides or multiplies by a negative number.

constraints: collect variables on the side that keeps the coefficient positive when possible
hints: Move variable terms to one side and constants to the other using the same operation on both sides.
Choose an arrangement that leaves a positive coefficient of x when possible.
Divide to isolate x, then test a convenient value to confirm which side of the boundary works.

constraints: at least -> >=; at most -> <=; more/fewer than -> strict
hints: Name the quantity described in the phrase with a variable.
Translate 'at least' as greater than or equal to, while 'at most' means less than or equal to.
Write the variable, comparison symbol, and stated number in the same order as the phrase.

constraints: one or two operations; do not solve
hints: Translate 'b times x' into a multiplication term before adding the extra amount.
Keep the phrase 'at most' as a comparison to the stated upper limit.
Write the relationship as an inequality and stop before trying to solve for x.

constraints: single constraint; state units where natural
hints: Read the symbol as a condition on the attendance-hour quantity.
The smallest qualifying whole amount occurs at the boundary because equality is included.
State that minimum with hours as its unit.

constraints: test one value against the graph or the symbols
hints: Test the given number in the first comparison and then in the second comparison.
For 'and', both comparisons must be true at the same time.
Use the two truth results to decide whether the number belongs to the overlap.

constraints: apply each operation to all three parts; one operation needed
hints: Apply the operation that removes the constant to all three parts of the chained inequality.
Keep the left, middle, and right comparisons together while you simplify.
Use parentheses for excluded endpoints and brackets for included endpoints when translating the final range.

constraints: solve each piece separately; keep the union
hints: Solve the left comparison and the right comparison as separate inequalities.
Keep each resulting ray; 'or' means a value may satisfy either one.
Write the two pieces as a union rather than looking for only their overlap.

constraints: keep operations balanced across all parts
hints: Treat the three-part inequality as one statement and apply every inverse operation to all three sections.
Subtract the constant, then divide each section by the positive coefficient.
Convert the two final bounds into interval notation with endpoint marks chosen from the inequality signs.

constraints: both inequality signs flip; rewrite smallest-to-largest
hints: First remove the added constant from all three sections.
Dividing every section by a negative reverses both comparison signs and reverses the order of the bounds.
Rewrite the final range from smallest to largest, then choose brackets or parentheses from inclusion.

constraints: each piece takes two steps; keep the union
hints: Solve each two-step comparison independently, using inverse operations in reverse order.
Keep the solution region from each comparison after isolating x.
Join the two regions with a union because 'or' accepts values from either region.
